sentences.text: Adult individuals of this pterosaur reached a wingspan of 0.9 meters.
Scientists have recovered three distinct specimens from the Kimmeridgian-age Solnhofen Limestone.
Unlike many relatives, the teeth stood vertically instead of lying horizontally.
A second, smaller fossil with a twenty-inch wingspan and partially ossified bones was identified as a juvenile.
Analysis of the eye sockets suggests the animal may have been active during the day.
August Goldfuss first described the species in 1831, initially misidentifying it as Pterodactylus crassirostris.
The specific name crassirostris translates to fat snout in Latin.
Johann Wagner established the genus Scaphognathus in 1861, naming it after the blunt shape of the lower jaws.
Its potential diurnal nature suggests niche partitioning with contemporary nocturnal pterosaurs like Ctenochasma and Rhamphorhynchus.
A 2013 phylogenetic analysis by Andres & Myers placed Scaphognathus within the rhamphorhynchid family tree.
Scaphognathus belongs to the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
The genus Scaphognathus is classified within the subfamily Scaphognathinae.
Scaphognathus lived in Germany during the Late Jurassic period.
Scaphognathus lived between 168.2 and 143.1 million years ago, from the Bathonian to the Tithonian stages.
